calibration_notes: Provisional-credit counting (039, 040, 041): Major in all three, which is consistent. The reviewers used different class labels for it (document_gap + hidden_ordering in 039/040, non_determinism in 041). The golds of 039/040/041/080/081 all apply one rule: count in-session filings, excluding the one being filed. The author notes disagree with that rule (080's notes say 'Rule is <=2 disputes eligible' and expect the third dispute denied, while its gold marks all three eligible). Sibling task_080/081, outside this group, rate that script/notes conflict Minor. If the 'count the current filing' reading is treated as document-supported, as the 041 finding allows, then 080/081 carry the same two-readings defect and may be under-rated. Their verifier should check this.

CLI-vs-dispute ordering (053, 054): Minor in both. logistics_007, a required document, says a pending dispute or replacement blocks the CLI, and both scripts accept the agent's order once told, so the gold order is what a document-following agent reaches.

Transfer-protocol presence-only ACTION grading (032, 033, 034, 035): Minor in all four, consistent with calibration's 'rules the grader cannot see'. 081's grading_basis_mismatch Minor (DB cannot see the 4th-request timing) is consistent with these.

Credit-card closure-reason classification, now compared exactly (045, 047, 048 crypto, 049 crypto): Minor in all four, which is internally consistent. In each case the first-stated reason or the scripted branch identifies the gold category, so an agent can resolve the inconsistency. task_043 has a weaker version (a 'simplifying my finances' aside after 'It's really just the annual fee'), and None is defensible there. If a later pass decides two-reason statements are 'two document-supported readings', all five should move together.

Unscripted expedited shipping (038, 039, 054): Minor in all three, matching calibration (documented 'strongly recommend expedited' for fraud matches the gold). 038 is the riskiest because the customer must accept a $10 Silver-tier fee unprompted.

Unscripted dispute resolution type: 039 Minor (the '$50 extra' fact fixes partial_refund 50), 040 and 041 Major (no document default, and the script facts point away from the gold's full_refund or exact 69.99). The difference has a stated reason and is consistent.

Multiple qualifying retention cards: 048 Major, while 045/047 dismiss the personal Platinum alternative. The stated reason differs: in 045/047 the customer already holds that card and asks for a business replacement. Consistent.

Customer transfer-request tool: only tasks 034, 049, 081-097 give the simulator request_human_agent_transfer (user_tools). In 049 the gold's single call is the natural response to the scripted 'Transfer me to a human agent.', so it is Minor (simulator reliability only). 082's opening request for a human is never pressed and its gold correctly has no call.
methodology_note: The review's grading model is accurate against the snapshot and the working-repo verified scorer. I re-ran the gold and 40-odd alternative trajectories through a harness built on the snapshot code with the gold-derived read_log_allowlist and a verbatim copy of _verified_db_match/_INPUT_ERROR_RE. Every replay result, gold index, DB value and quote cited in these 20 findings reproduced, apart from one heading-and-bullet merge in 032. The reasoning is sound and applies calibration well for the recurring classes. Its blind spots are cross-task: it rated the CLI-before-dispute ordering Major in 053 but missed it in 054, and in 046 it described an undocumented 'stop at the first failed check' convention but rated it Minor. The 'most agents will...' probability judgments are the least verifiable part of the method; where the review's own mechanism matched calibration's Major definition, I followed the definition. One grading-model point I did not re-check in code: that the customer's tool results are hidden from the agent. Nothing in this group depends on it beyond 053, where the conclusion does not need it.
